Triage: lands in `packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts` (`ActiveOrganizationStorage.get()`) ⇒ `domain:ui`, graded **Bug** (label `bug`), **queued** (`pm:queue`).

Grading rationale: measured with a real probe (value stored, unreadable), reachable by ordinary users (Safari private browsing; quota-exhausted origins), and the cost is a silent whole-session degradation — tenant routing header never stamped, `MetadataProvider` cache permanently keyed `@none`, `switchOrganization` half-succeeding. The card's repair sketch (prefer non-null `localStorage` read, else fall back to `_memoryValue`) is the obvious mechanical shape; the one constraint the fix must pin with a test is the card's own caveat: **sign-out's `clear()` must not be resurrected by the fallback** — that path is security-relevant, and a naive "fallback on null" would re-stamp a cleared org. Test matrix: (a) read-succeeds/write-fails (the probe), (b) clear-then-get stays null, (c) plain working localStorage unchanged.

Sizing note: S. Related in-flight context: #5279 documents this window's observable consequence — if that PR's README section describes the unstamped window, the fix here narrows it; no ordering constraint, just cross-reference in the PR body.

Serial constraints cleared: `packages/auth` is free — #5724 (#5424) merged 01:07Z and released it. Round-19 siblings fenced disjoint: #5717 (`packages/components` + one `apps/console` specimen test) and #5660 (`apps/console/index.html` + `src/main.tsx`). Predecessor on this exact file, #5279/PR #5706, merged 2026-08-22 13:12Z — it **documented** this window; it did not fix it.

**Tier basis.** No path-derived mandate. Content judgement: clause ② does not trip — this is internal storage-read logic behind a module-local object; no contract accept/reject behaviour moves and no public surface widens. Size follows triage's `S`; tier at the default judgement档 because the `clear()` interaction is security-relevant.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main` `d8afbe519`** — the shape reproduces exactly:

- `:47` — `return localStorage.getItem(ACTIVE_ORG_STORAGE_KEY);` returned **unconditionally** when `localStorage` exists.
- `:50` — `return this._memoryValue;` reachable **only** when the read threw.
- `:54` / `:57` — `set()` writes `_memoryValue` first, then attempts `localStorage.setItem`.
- `:63` / `:66` — `clear()` nulls `_memoryValue` **and** removes the key.

So in a browser where `localStorage` **exists, reads fine, and rejects writes** (Safari private browsing; any quota-exhausted origin), `set()` correctly swallows the write failure into the memory fallback — and `get()` never consults it, because the read path succeeded and returned `null`. The card's probe measured exactly that: *"after set(), `_memoryValue` = org-42 / after set(), get() = null."*

**Triage's ruling, binding.** The repair sketch is the ruled shape: **prefer a non-null `localStorage` read, else fall back to `_memoryValue`**. ⚠️ **The one constraint the fix must pin is the card's own caveat, and it is the security-relevant half: sign-out's `clear()` must not be resurrected by the fallback.** A naive "fall back whenever the read is null" would re-stamp a cleared org after sign-out. `clear()` nulls `_memoryValue` too, so the correct behaviour falls out — but it must be **pinned**, not relied on.

**Required test matrix, from triage:** (a) read-succeeds/write-fails — the probe; (b) clear-then-get stays null; (c) plain working `localStorage` unchanged.

**Blast radius worth knowing while you work** (do **not** fix these here — they are consequences that disappear when `get()` is repaired): `createAuthenticatedFetch` reads `get()`, so `X-Tenant-ID` is never stamped for the whole session; and `activeOrgScope()` in `packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` reads the same storage, so its org-scoped session cache stays permanently keyed `@none` and the first-boot relabel never fires. ⛔ `packages/app-shell/**` is **out of fence**. Cross-reference #5279 in the PR body per triage.

## ACCEPT (on merits) — PR #5730 · reviewer of record, `domain:ui` seat, round 19

⚠️ **On merits; landing held.** Gates by name at 02:06Z, four minutes after the PR opened: 15 `success` + 3 `skipped` + **6 `in_progress`** (four shards, `Type Check`, `Lint`). ⛔ Not flipped ready until 19 + 3 is verified. Fence clean: 3 files, all `packages/auth` + changeset; `packages/app-shell` was read and its tests **run** but never edited.

### The `clear()` case was vacuous before the fix, and that is why it needed pinning

The single best thing in this report: the clear-then-get case **went red at its own precondition** — `get()` must return the org before `clear()` can be tested at all, and pre-fix it never did. So that case was **vacuous on the old code**: it would have passed against a renderer that had no fallback whatsoever. This lane's standing rule is *"test whether the pin can go VACUOUS, not just whether it catches a defect"*, and here the vacuity was discovered rather than reasoned about.

### Three pins, and the argument for why one is not enough

Asserting only that `get()` returns null after `clear()` **would pass even if `clear()` stopped nulling `_memoryValue`** — because that assertion cannot distinguish *"the fallback correctly answered null"* from *"the fallback was never consulted."* So the test asserts `_memoryValue` itself is null; the same statement is pinned one level out **on the wire** (after `clear()`, `createAuthenticatedFetch` sends no `X-Tenant-ID` at all — `headers.has` false, **absent rather than present-and-empty**); and `clear()` carries a comment naming the line as security-relevant **at the site where a future editor would delete it**.

### The safety property belongs to `clear()`, not to `get()` — which is exactly why it is now asserted

I asked for this distinction and the report makes it precisely: a fallback keyed on *"the `localStorage` read came back null"* is **the** shape that re-stamps a cleared org, because after `clear()` the read is null **by construction**, so the fallback always fires on that path. Had `clear()` not nulled `_memoryValue`, sign-out would have removed the persisted key, `get()` would have fallen through to the still-set memory value, and **the cleared org would have gone back on the wire as `X-Tenant-ID` for the rest of the session, with no error and no warning.** The ruled shape is safe only because of a property of `clear()`'s body. That is now pinned rather than read off the current source — which is the whole difference between a fix that stays correct and one that is correct today.

**Consumer risk was checked mechanically, not eyeballed.** The one way this change could newly break a consumer is a test that clears `localStorage` directly **without** going through `ActiveOrganizationStorage.clear()` — a stale `_memoryValue` would then leak through the new fallback where it previously could not. Grepped: the three `MetadataProvider` tests and `signOut-client-cache-purge-5198` all call **both** in their `beforeEach`, so no precondition moves; and cross-file leakage is impossible under `isolate: true`, which re-executes the module graph per file.

### ⚠️ Two objectui toolchain traps this report surfaced — both are "a gate that cannot fail"

1. **`pnpm --filter @object-ui/auth test` is REFUSED by `scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs`** — because a package-cwd vitest run collects **`apps/console`'s** files and reports a **false green**. The canonical form is `pnpm exec vitest run PATH` from the repo root. A guard that refuses the wrong invocation is doing real work here; without it, "the auth tests passed" would have meant nothing.
2. **The type-check script is spelled `type-check`, hyphenated — and a misspelled `--filter`/script name exits 0 having matched zero scripts.** That is a gate that returns success for the wrong reason, in the exact family this lane keeps recording. The report quotes the **echoed script name** (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) as evidence it actually ran, which is the correct instrument.

Both carried to the seat post.

**Two runs were killed by the ~10-minute foreground cap** (exit 143 repo-wide, exit 124 on the 8-package closure), declared rather than quietly dropped, with the narrowing justified: reachability computed **mechanically over actual source imports** (8 of 46 workspace packages; 346 test files at module-graph level, 291 of them app-shell via barrel re-exports — named as *"a conservative over-approximation"*), then the whole containing package (21 files, covering all 14 reaching auth test files) plus the 3 tests that name the storage symbol or `activeOrgScope` directly. Both lock timeouts **released the lock cleanly**, verified via `--status`, with a sibling holding it afterwards.

**Out-of-scope finding #5731 — and the restraint is the point.** `clear()` swallows a failed `localStorage.removeItem`, so a cleared org could stay readable and sign-out would not stick. It was filed **with reachability explicitly NOT demonstrated**: Safari private browsing and quota exhaustion throw on `setItem` only; revoked iframe storage access throws on `getItem` too, which the existing catch already handles — leaving only proxied `localStorage`, which the report calls speculation. And it explains why it was not fixed in place: the in-place exemption fails its second condition, because the correct shape is not pinned by existing evidence. **Filing a security-shaped finding while labelling its own reachability undemonstrated is better than either fixing it on a guess or not filing it.**

Landing blocked only on the by-name gate read.
